items.title: Take a StoryWalk®: Outdoor reading adventures await in Mississauga parks
items.summary: Turn a walk in the park into an illustrated storybook adventure. Families can read, explore and get active year-round at four Mississauga parks Adventure is waiting. Just follow the pages. Residents are invited to discover StoryWalk®, a free outdoor experience that transforms select park trails across Mississauga into interactive reading adventures. Combining literacy, outdoor recreation and active living, StoryWalk® encourages residents to explore their community and foster a love of reading. Illustrated pages from select children’s books are posted on signs along walking paths at four parks. These stories have been selected by Mississauga Library staff and reflect diverse, family-friendly themes told with colourful illustrations, making the experience enjoyable for readers of all ages and reading levels. Each participating location features a different story by a Canadian author, encouraging families to explore new parks and discover a unique reading adventure at every stop: StoryWalk® trails are available year-round during regular park hours. The trails are accessible and maintained through all seasons, allowing residents to enjoy the experience anytime and at their own pace. Visit a participating park, breathe in some fresh air and watch a story come to life with every step. Read. Walk. Repeat! When the trails end, the tales continue at Mississauga Library.

items.title: Mississauga residents back subway extension, but few confident it will actually be built
items.summary: A majority of Mississauga residents support bringing subway service to downtown, but a new survey suggests there is far less agreement over whether it should take priority over improved GO service. A survey of 1,000 Mississauga residents found 65 per cent support extending subway service to downtown Mississauga near Square One, while 20 per cent oppose the idea and 15 per cent are unsure. But when residents were asked to choose between a subway extension and all-day, two-way GO train service on the Milton line, the result was almost evenly divided. Forty-five per cent picked the subway as the better transit investment, while 44 per cent chose expanded Milton GO service. Another 11 per cent were unsure. The survey was conducted by Liaison Strategies between Oct. 2 and Oct. 4, shortly after the subway proposal was raised during the Mississauga mayoral campaign. The poll found an even bigger gap between support for the subway and confidence that it will actually be built. Only 19 per cent of respondents said they were very or somewhat confident a subway extension would eventually be constructed. Four per cent were very confident and 15 per cent somewhat confident. Meanwhile, 61 per cent said they were either not very or not at all confident the project would be built, while 20 per cent were unsure.

items.title: 49-Year-Old Mississauga Man Faces 11 Charges After Sarnia Raid Turns Up Loaded Handgun, Drugs
items.summary: According to Insauga, a 49-year-old Mississauga man is facing multiple drug and firearms charges after Sarnia police searched a home in the 1700 block of London Line on Oct. 6 and seized a loaded handgun along with an estimated $16,000 worth of drugs. The Sarnia Police Service Drug Unit carried out the search with help from the force's Intelligence Unit and Emergency Response Team. Officers seized a loaded Taurus 9mm handgun along with additional ammunition during the raid, in addition to the suspected drugs. Police have not released the accused's name, but Insauga reports he faces 11 charges in total, including possession of a prohibited firearm, possession of a firearm while prohibited, possession of ammunition while prohibited, and possession of a firearm without a licence. He is also charged with carrying a concealed weapon, carrying a weapon for a dangerous purpose, and trafficking-related offences involving cocaine and methamphetamine. Police additionally laid a charge of possession of property obtained by crime.

items.title: Kenneth Law case: Families reveal the devastating toll in 'The Poison Seller'
items.summary: Mississauga’s Kenneth Law pleaded guilty to aiding suicide after selling lethal chemicals online to people around the world. A CBC investigation linked Law to at least 147 deaths, but the real number might never be known. The Poison Seller, a documentary from The Passionate Eye, examines the investigation that left families asking why police didn't halt his operations sooner, and the CBC’s Kelda Yuen sat down with the filmmaking team behind it. If you or someone you know is struggling, help is available. In Canada, you can call or text 988 to reach the Suicide Crisis Helpline. Kids Help Phone is available at 1-800-668-6868, or by texting 686868.

items.title: Peel Police Say Ridgeway Plaza Topped the List for Stunt-Driving Tickets This Summer
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police visited Mississauga's Ridgeway Plaza and the nearby Auto Spa area 26 times to lay charges during their latest Project ERASE crackdown, more than any other hot spot in the region. The enforcement campaign, aimed at eliminating street racing and stunt driving, ran from May 1 through the end of August and also involved the Ontario Provincial Police along with municipal forces in Toronto, Durham, Halton and Hamilton. The figures, presented last week to the City of Mississauga's Road Safety Committee, covered enforcement action taken only in Mississauga and Brampton. Peel police Const. Claudia D'Amico told committee members officers targeted the specific locations that residents have been complaining about. Ridgeway Plaza has drawn complaints and headlines since it opened in 2022 over late-night noise, street racing and parking problems. Insauga reports police also conducted enforcement 22 times in the Financial Plaza area of north Meadowvale, another part of the city known for illegal street racing and dangerous driving.

items.title: Nearly 150 Residents Turn Out to Grill Five Ward 3 Candidates on Taxes and Bloor Street Redesign
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, nearly 150 residents attended a Ward 3 candidates meeting on Oct. 5, where five council hopefuls, Kim Pines, Mendi Kabashi, Chris Fonseca, Arshad Hashmi and Stjepan Vukovic, fielded questions on property taxes, the Bloor Street redesign project and public safety in the Applewood and Rockwood neighbourhoods. The event was co-hosted by the Applewood Hills and Heights Residents' Association and the Rockwood Residents' Association, and was held at Sts. Martha and Mary Parish Catholic Church. Resident Pedro Coronado, who has lived in the ward for nearly 10 years, told the outlet he already knew who he wanted to vote for before the meeting, but said attending solidified his decision. Coronado said he voted differently in the last municipal election, explaining that rising costs over the past five years changed his thinking this time around. Mississauga.com reports sisters Lorraine Katanik and Kathy Klas arrived undecided and left with enough information to make up their minds. The meeting is one of several ward-level candidate forums being held across Mississauga ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election.

items.title: Where do Mississauga mayoral candidates stand on e-scooters, road safety and cycling infrastructure?
items.summary: Mayoral candidates outline their plans for e-scooter enforcement, road safety and cycling infrastructure. Although legal in Mississauga, enforcement for e-scooter and e-bike violations falls under the jurisdiction of Peel Regional Police under the Highway Traffic Act. Ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election, we asked mayoral candidates how they will address road safety, rising concerns around e-scooters and cycling infrastructure. Candidates were asked to respond in 200 words to each of those issues, with the following question: With rising concerns over road safety, e-scooter injuries, and cycling infrastructure — and following the provincial ban on speed cameras — what specific actions will you take as mayor to improve street safety and ensure cycling and road projects deliver measurable results for taxpayers? Here’s what they said in email statements. Responses have been edited for length. Candidate did not provide a response by publication deadline. E-scooters: Safety comes first. I would review the city’s current approach, strengthen designated operating and parking areas, improve education and enforcement, and work with Peel police and health care partners to respond to the rise in injuries.

items.title: Global Tooling Firm Ceratizit Relocates Its Canadian Head Office to Mississauga's Airport Corporate Centre
items.summary: According to Advanced Manufacturing, Ceratizit has moved its Canadian headquarters to a new facility in Mississauga's Airport Corporate Centre at 2425 Matheson Blvd. East. The company said the site was chosen for its easy access to Toronto Pearson International Airport and major highways including the 401, 407 and 427. Ceratizit of Canada Tooling Solutions ULC will run the company's Canadian sales, technical support and customer service operations for manufacturers from the new location. The company said the move supports its broader push on quality, sustainability and regulatory compliance across its operations. Ceratizit also pointed to its vertically integrated tungsten supply network, including Global Tungsten and Powders, which it said gives it control over every stage of tungsten processing, from raw material conversion through to high-purity ammonium paratungstate production. The company said that integration helps secure its supply chain and keep material quality consistent for manufacturers making critical components.
